title: Dragoon Swordsman
text: “That’s way too dramatic.”
“Raised as a dragon’s adopted child, learning combat under a hero’s protection… that backstory alone could make a whole story. Sounds like they could even become a Seven Star Hero someday.”
Not entirely wrong, I say. Assistant did eventually become the Seven Star Hero of the Whip, after all. Well, it was furious about being turned into a shield by Doctor and hated the whole thing.
“If it were the ‘gets killed’ pattern… learning swordsmanship and becoming some ace magic swordsman, maybe? No, wait, since it’s a girl, a great sorceress… a witch works nicely too.”
“…Kuro would probably love that. Could that backstory be turned into a shield? Existence of a different fate, becoming a Dragoon Swordsman or something—if we just whisper that kind of setup…”
“Ren… what kind of kid are you?”

Would Assistant really burn with vengeance along that kind of storyline? Either way, I think it was the sorcerer route. As for Rival’s tale—and my memory here is quite hazy—I recall that in the loop where they stayed in Melromarc, Ren went berserk, and Assistant cast a curse to stop it.
“No wait, Kuro was a Filolial too. Then that backstory wouldn’t apply.”
Kuro-chan probably hates dragons, if I had to guess.
“Still, I do appreciate Iwatani-sama’s decisiveness in relying on this, but it’s awfully self-serving, isn’t it? I do wonder if it’s really okay to decide something like that so easily.”
“That dragon, you know—turns out it’s got a worrywart streak buried in there somewhere. Seems like it’s planning to change its shape and secretly join up with us.”
“Eh? Really?”
“Yeah. Said to come back to that spot later. Oh, and don’t tell Wyndia-chan, okay?”
“Ohh!”
“Keel-kun, you absolutely cannot tell her, okay? You seem like the type who’d blab.”
“Got it, big bro! Oh, but I can tell Raphtalia-chan and the others, right?”

So it’s going to be this kind of flow after all, I say. There was a time it possessed some egg or another belonging to Rival and tagged along to keep watch. So it’ll probably try to possess Rival, who’s already hatched, or something along those lines. Whether that’s even possible, I have no idea.
“Father. Dragons are unnecessary, I say!”

Assistant alone would be one thing, but Rival’s parent is entirely unnecessary, I say! To begin with, at a time when there’s already a strong chance Rival is lurking around some nest somewhere, if this thing carelessly comes near me and Rival multiplies, there’ll be no living with it. And on top of that, we currently already have Rafumi, a nuisance on par with Rival, I say.

“I get why Motoyasu-kun and the Filolials wouldn’t like it, but when things play out this way and we get asked… well, I figure it’s fine as long as it just lives peacefully in Lars-chan’s village instead of the circus.”
“Iwatani-sama, at this point, wouldn’t it be fine to just have the slaves settle permanently in that village instead of rebuilding it?”
“Theo, don’t say something that defeats the whole purpose. Think about how Shion and Raphtalia-chan would feel.”
Crocodile Guy’s hometown is the neighboring town, I say. It seems Rabbit Guy hasn’t quite grasped how important that place is, being more focused on efficiency.
Crocodile Guy stayed silent, but his face made it clear he couldn’t agree with Rabbit Guy’s suggestion.
“You’re right. Shion, I’m sorry.”
“…Don’t worry about it. I understand it’s an outrageous wish.”
“Ah, you’re back.”
Right on cue, Rafumi showed up, I say. Then, after casually peeking into the carriage, it turned toward Father with an expression that said “obviously.”
“Hey. Don’t tell me you knew something about this?”
Ren, suspicious, pressed Rafumi.
“If you’re asking whether I had any inkling, then yes, I did, to be precise.”
“Then why’d you stay quiet?”
Ren, practically radiating hostility, glared at Rafumi and readied his sword.
“Hmph, Azott. Do you really think I’d go around blabbing at a time like this? I’m not so tasteless as to do something that dull.”
“If you’d said something, it wouldn’t have blown up into this much of a mess!”
“That’s exactly why I kept things at the village down to a mere precautionary check, so it wouldn’t turn into that much of a fuss.”
“Ah, so that’s why the scale of the commotion was smaller.”
“Guh…”
“I figured you’d find out the results eventually either way. All within expectations. Saint Windy has joined, then.”
“Hey, wait, what’s with that name?! What happened to that kid to give her a name like that?! Explain!”
“The secret of Saint Windy iiis—”
Just as Rafumi was about to answer, Ren turned his back as if ignoring her entirely.
“Hey, what’s with that attitude, listen!”
“You weren’t going to tell me anyway! I’m just not engaging!”
“Fine then. The third Melfilo—Saint Windy.”
“What is that, some catchphrase for a new warrior debuting in a girls’ anime? What even is a Melfilo?”
“A Melfilo is, welll—”
As usual, it seemed determined to play coy and drag things out as though it had no intention of ever explaining.
“Forget it, you clearly have no intention of telling me. It’s all vague in the end anyway, and given how deliberately cryptic you’re being, Rafumi-chan, you’re more trouble than Motoyasu-kun.”

Should I be the one to spoil the secret here, I say? It was a heroic warrior that Filo-tan and Fiancée performed together. But since it’s a transformation done using a compact Rival developed, whether I actually want to explain it is a bit questionable, I say. Ah, but Filo-tan’s transformation scene really was lovely, I must say.

“More trouble than Spear Hero is quite the affront—I’m simply saying it’s bad manners for you heroes to all so casually want spoilers. There’s no strategy guide to life, originally. Isn’t it precisely because the future is uncertain that it’s good?”
“I get what you’re trying to say, but in your case, you know things and then tease people about it, so I think that’s the actual problem…”
“There are things even I don’t know. To begin with, I never expected the dragon crowd to end up joining in like this.”

Well, I too knew that Assistant and Rival’s parent were around, but I never imagined that Assistant, drawn in by the lively atmosphere, would come play here just because a circus happened to visit this village, I say.

“Guess it’s down to how you meet someone… in the original history, it seems Ren really messed things up, and thinking about how much worse things were for Wyndia-chan back then, I suppose this is for the best?”
“If anything, considering it turned into a rescue mission despite the misunderstanding, you could call it a rather curious encounter, I say.”

Rushing off to the mountains to rescue someone you think has been kidnapped by a monster is plenty unexpected in its own right, I say. Ren has a tendency to be adored by those younger than him, after all. It seems to be the natural flow of things that he ends up looking after juniors with excessive care.
“Motoyasu-kun, I’d appreciate it if you considered the possibilities a little more…”
“I figured he’d be holed up in his den a lot more than this, I say.”
“No amount of talking about where the blame lies is going to solve anything, so it can’t be helped. Motoyasu-kun, please bear with it this time.”
Guh… I say. If Rival really shows up as-is, I won’t be able to go anywhere near it, so I’ll need to keep my distance with everything I’ve got, I say.
“Sounds like our forces are steadily growing, huh… no, wait, I do wonder if it’s really fine to have a dragon join us after getting beaten that thoroughly.”
“If anything, it’s more that Wyndia-chan’s watchdog is coming, and we’ve already worked out that it’ll cover childcare expenses too.”
“A slave trader collecting babysitting fees from a dragon—what a strange experience. Sounds like it could be a book.”

Father gave a wry smile at Rabbit Guy’s words. And so, the commotion that broke out in the eastern village came to a settling point. Guh… this is exactly why I didn’t want to come anywhere near here, I say.

And so, once it turned to deep night… Father, myself, Ren, and the men Father had picked out—Wolf, Crocodile Guy, and Rabbit Guy—headed to the meeting spot with Rival’s parent. The Filolial-samas were asked to stay behind and watch the place, so they remained on standby.
“It’s rare for even Ren to come along.”
“If things go well, maybe I can get Kuro and Luna to stop coming near me. Judging by their reactions, I want their cooperation.”
“No matter what happens, you will be Kuro-chan and Luna-chan’s playmate, I say!”
“I already said I don’t want to.”
Ren really doesn’t know when to give up, I say. More importantly, what exactly is he expecting from Rival’s parent, I wonder?
